source.author: stat
source.text: dixerat; atque illi sese deus obtulit ultro turbidus imbre genas et nube natantis harenae, nec saevit dictis, trunca sed pectora quercu ter quater oppositi, quantum ira deusque valebat, impulit assurgens: tandem vestigia flexit excussumque manu tegimen, conversaque lente terga refert, instant undae sequiturque labantem amnis ovans; nec non saxis et grandine ferri desuper infestant Tyrii geminoque repellunt aggere, quid faciat bellis obsessus et undis?
source.text_original: ' / dixerat; atque illi sese deus obtulit ultro / turbidus imbre genas et nube natantis harenae, / nec saevit dictis, trunca sed pectora quercu / ter quater oppositi, quantum ira deusque valebat, / impulit assurgens: tandem vestigia flexit / excussumque manu tegimen, conversaque lente / terga refert, instant undae sequiturque labantem / amnis ovans; nec non saxis et grandine ferri / desuper infestant Tyrii geminoque repellunt / aggere, quid faciat bellis obsessus et undis?
source.text_english: He had spoken; and straightway the god presented himself to him, turbulent, with cheeks wet from rain and with a cloud of sand drifting about him, and he did not rage with words, but, setting his broken breast against the oak, he thrust himself three and four times against them, as far as anger and a god could avail; then at last he turned his steps and, shaking off with his hand the covering, with his back now turned slowly, he carries it away; the waves press on, and the river, exulting, follows him as he staggers. And furthermore the Tyrians attack him from above with rocks and hail of iron, and repel him with a double rampart: what is he to do, besieged by war and by waves?

reuse.text: excussi manibus remi, conversaque frontem puppis in oblicum resonos latus accipit ictus, vela super tremulum subitus volitantia malum turbo rapit.
reuse.text_original: excussi manibus remi, conversaque frontem / puppis in oblicum resonos latus accipit ictus, / vela super tremulum subitus volitantia malum / turbo rapit.
reuse.text_english: The oars were struck from their hands, and the ship, its prow turned askew, receives the echoing blows on its side; then a sudden whirlwind snatches the sails, fluttering above, from the trembling mast.
